To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the lipid A precursor of Escherichia coli K12 contains four 3-hy-droxymyristic acid residues and is heterogeneously substituted by phosphorylethanol-amine, polyamines and 4-amino-4-deoxy-l-arabinose.
the lipid A of lipopolysacharides is not a homogeneous compound but a heterogeneous mixture of closely related structures.
the lipid A of Salmonella minnesota R 595 is composed of glucosamine 1-phosphate disaccharides substituted by 3-hydroxy-myristic acid and 3-hydroxoctadecanoic acid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of lipid A intermediates and the elucidation of the mechanism of lipid A biosynthesis in Salmonella typhimurium.

the elucidation of the chemical structures of the lipid A intermediates accumulated in a mutant strain of Salmonella typhimurium LT-2, which has a conditional requirement for 3-deoxy-D-manno-octa-2-ulopyranosonic acid (kdo).
the elucidation of the biosynthetic pathway of lipid A.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the lipid A precursor of the mutants accumulates at the restrictive temperature in the form of at least three different species, which can be distinguished by the presence of phosphorylethanolamin, 4-amino-4-deoxy-L-arabinose and the polyamines.
the lipid A structure of Salmonella lipopolysac-charides is a mixture of at least three different species.
the neutral precursor is the precursor of the acidic precursor and the latter the precursor of the complete lipid A.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lipid A biosynthesis proceeds via a neutral and an acidic precursor, which differ in their chemical structure and the way of their synthesis.

the lipid A biosynthesis is a multistep process, in which the first step involves the synthesis of the acidic precursor and the subsequent addition of phosphorylethanolamines and polyamines leads to the neutral precursor.

we have now identified the complete lipid A biosynthesis pathway and that the final step of this pathway is the addition of 4-amido-4-deoxy-l-arabinose, phosphoryl-ethanolamine and polyamino compounds to the acidic precursor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now identify the 4-amino-4-deoxy-l-arabinose residue as an important component in the biosynthesis and structure of the lipid A moiety of the lipopolysacchrides of Salmonella typhimurium LT2.
the neutral lipid A precursor is the immediate precursor of the complete lipopolysacchride structure.
we have identified a new lipid A structure, and we have identified a mutant that accumulates it.
